docs.text: dot-response-header dot-response-header is Dotkernel's middleware for setting and overwriting custom response headers. Documentation Documentation is available at: https://docs.dotkernel.org/dot-response-header/. Versions Version Supported PHP 4.x :white_check_mark: 8.3 to 8.6 3.x Security fixes only 8.2 to 8.5 <= 2.x :x: Upgrading from 3.x? See Upgrading to 4.x . Badges Requirements PHP : 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 or 8.6 Installation Run the following command in your project root directory: composer require dotkernel/dot-response-header Next, register the package's ConfigProvider to your application config. Dot\ResponseHeader\ConfigProvider::class, Make sure to register the package under the // DK packages section. After registering the package, add it to the middleware stack in config/pipeline.php after $app->pipe(RouteMiddleware::class); $app->pipe(RouteMiddleware::class); $app->pipe(\Dot\ResponseHeader\Middleware\ResponseHeaderMiddleware::class); Create a new file response-header.global.php in config/autoload with the below configuration array: <?php return [ 'dot_response_headers' => [ '*' => [ 'CustomHeader1' => [ 'value' => 'CustomHeader1-Value', 'overwrite' => true, ], 'CustomHeader2' => [ 'value' => 'CustomHeader2-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], 'home' => [ 'CustomHeader' => [ 'value' => 'header3', ], ], 'login' => [ 'LoginHeader' => [ 'value' => 'LoginHeader-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], ], ]; Because headers are matched with route names, we can have custom response headers for every request, by defining new headers under the * key. All headers under * will be set for every response. To add response headers for a specific route, define a new array using the exact route name as the array key. Example: 'dot_response_headers' => [ 'user' => [ 'UserCustomHeader' => [ 'value' => 'UserCustomHeader-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], ], // This will set a new header named UserCustomHeader with the UserCustomHeader-Value value for the route named 'user' To overwrite an existing header use overwrite => true . The * headers are applied before the route headers, so a route header replaces a * header with the same name only when it sets overwrite => true . An invalid configuration throws Dot\ResponseHeader\Exception\InvalidConfigException when the middleware is created, with a message naming the key.

docs.text: Usage Because headers are matched with route names, we can have custom response headers for every request, by defining new headers under the * key, in the configuration file response-header.global.php . All headers under * will be set for every response. To add response headers for a specific set of routes, define a new array using the route name as the array key. Example 'dot_response_headers' => [ 'user' => [ 'UserCustomHeader' => [ 'value' => 'UserCustomHeader-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], ], // This will set a new header named UserCustomHeader with the UserCustomHeader-Value value for any route name matching 'user' To overwrite an existing header use overwrite => true .

docs.text: Configuration Requirements PHP : 8.3, 8.4, 8.5 or 8.6 mezzio/mezzio-router : 3.x or 4.x (PHP 8.6 needs 4.3 or newer) Register ConfigProvider Next, register the package's ConfigProvider to your application config. Dot\ResponseHeader\ConfigProvider::class, Make sure to register the package under the // DK packages section. Add the package to the middleware stack After registering the package, add it to the middleware stack in config/pipeline.php after $app->pipe(RouteMiddleware::class); $app->pipe(RouteMiddleware::class); $app->pipe(\Dot\ResponseHeader\Middleware\ResponseHeaderMiddleware::class); If the middleware is piped before RouteMiddleware , no route is known yet and only the * headers are added. Add configuration in autoload Create a new file response-header.global.php in config/autoload with the below configuration array: <?php return [ 'dot_response_headers' => [ '*' => [ 'CustomHeader1' => [ 'value' => 'CustomHeader1-Value', 'overwrite' => true, ], 'CustomHeader2' => [ 'value' => 'CustomHeader2-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], 'home' => [ 'CustomHeader' => [ 'value' => 'header3', ], ], 'login' => [ 'LoginHeader' => [ 'value' => 'LoginHeader-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], ], ]; Configuration keys Key Type Default Meaning dot_response_headers array required Route name (or * ) to headers. An empty array is allowed and adds no headers <route>.<header>.value string, int, float or a non-empty list of strings none Header value. Numbers are sent as strings; a list sends one header with several values. An entry without value is skipped <route>.<header>.overwrite bool false Replace the header if the response already has it Invalid configuration The configuration is checked once, when the container creates the middleware. A wrong type throws Dot\ResponseHeader\Exception\InvalidConfigException with a message naming the key, for example: dot_response_headers.*.X-Frame-Options.overwrite must be a bool, int given. A missing config service or a missing dot_response_headers key also throws InvalidConfigException .

docs.text: Upgrading to 4.x dot-response-header 4.x keeps the 3.x configuration format. A valid 3.x configuration sends the same headers in 4.x. Most applications only need to bump the version constraint. composer require dotkernel/dot-response-header:^4.0 Changes that can break your code Change Symptom Fix PHP 8.2 support dropped Composer refuses to install Upgrade to PHP 8.3 or newer overwrite must be a bool InvalidConfigException: dot_response_headers.<route>.<header>.overwrite must be a bool, int given. Use true or false . In 3.x, 1 or 'true' were silently treated as false Route and header entries must be arrays InvalidConfigException naming the key In 3.x a string route entry was ignored with a PHP warning, and a string header entry threw a TypeError on every request value must be a string, a number or a non-empty list of strings InvalidConfigException naming the key In 3.x null threw from the PSR-7 implementation on every request The factory throws Dot\ResponseHeader\Exception\InvalidConfigException instead of Exception Code that catches Exception still works; code that compares the exact class does not Catch InvalidArgumentException or InvalidConfigException ConfigProvider and ResponseHeaderMiddlewareFactory are final Class ... cannot extend final class Decorate them or write your own factory. ResponseHeaderMiddleware is not final Changes in behaviour Change Effect What to do Configuration is checked when the middleware is created Errors appear once, with the key in the message, instead of on each request Nothing 'dot_response_headers' => [] is allowed In 3.x it threw Unable to find dot-response-header config. ; now no headers are added Nothing A config service that implements ArrayAccess is accepted In 3.x it threw a TypeError Nothing Numeric values are sent as strings 3600 becomes "3600" , as before with Laminas Diactoros Nothing mezzio/mezzio-router 4.x is allowed PHP 8.6 installs router 4.3 or newer Nothing

docs.text: Usage Because headers are matched with route names, we can have custom response headers for every request, by defining new headers under the * key, in the configuration file response-header.global.php . All headers under * will be set for every response, including 404 and 405 responses. To add response headers for a specific route, define a new array using the route name as the array key. The key must be the exact route name; it is not a pattern. Example 'dot_response_headers' => [ 'user' => [ 'UserCustomHeader' => [ 'value' => 'UserCustomHeader-Value', 'overwrite' => false, ], ], ], // This will set a new header named UserCustomHeader with the UserCustomHeader-Value value for the route named 'user' Overwriting headers Headers are applied in this order: The response returned by the handler. The * headers. The headers of the matched route. A header that already exists is only replaced when its entry has 'overwrite' => true . This also applies between steps 2 and 3: a route header replaces a * header with the same name only when it sets 'overwrite' => true . 'dot_response_headers' => [ '*' => [ 'Cache-Control' => [ 'value' => 'no-store', ], ], 'image' => [ 'Cache-Control' => [ 'value' => 'public, max-age=86400', 'overwrite' => true, ], ], ], // The 'image' route gets "Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400", every other route gets "Cache-Control: no-store" Header names are case-insensitive, so x-custom set by a handler counts as an existing X-Custom header. Header values A value can be a string, a number or a list of strings: 'dot_response_headers' => [ '*' => [ 'Access-Control-Max-Age' => [ 'value' => 3600, ], 'Vary' => [ 'value' => ['Accept', 'Origin'], ], ], ],
